statement: For any finite prime set I and any prescribed signs epsilon_p, there exists a unique coprime class M modulo product(I) such that M*product(I)/p is congruent to epsilon_p modulo p for every p in I.
closes: all proposed contradictions using only distinct top primes and an arbitrary common lower multiplier
dependency_gaps: A closing proof must exploit that the common multiplier is the exact lower-prime-power part of lcm(1,...,n).
No distribution theorem for that specific multiplier across primes in (n/2,n] is known here.
The first public question was not advanced.
